oewn-02344167-v.learner: to be the cause of something, or the thing that it comes from.
examples: He immediately offered to fetch her others; all that his library afforded.
I hope at least it will not afford you any displeasure.

oewn-02750326-v.learner: to have enough money to do something or to buy something.
examples: They could not afford a carriage of their own.

oewn-01195161-v.learner: to be able to spare something, or to be able to give it up.
examples: With so few servants, she could not afford to lose even one.

oewn-00989103-v.learner: to say what someone or something is like.
examples: You will find her manners beyond anything I can describe
I never saw such capacity, and taste, and application, and elegance, as you describe

oewn-00967067-v.learner: to give an account of something in words.
examples: They could describe an entertainment with accuracy, relate an anecdote with humour
I described and enforced them earnestly.

oewn-01585566-v.learner: to make a mark or a line on a surface.
examples: The skater described a wide circle on the ice.

oewn-01141382-s.learner: unpleasant to be with or to deal with.
examples: he is a most disagreeable, horrid man, not at all worth pleasing
I have spent four days in the same house with him, and I think him very disagreeable.
It was a disagreeable situation, and she wished herself at home.

oewn-00563624-s.learner: not fitting what you like or what you expected.
examples: She found the task disagreeable and put it aside.

oewn-00089896-r.learner: to a great degree, or in a way that shows a good opinion and much respect.
examples: He was quite young, wonderfully handsome, extremely agreeable
Such a countenance, such manners, and so extremely accomplished for her age!
his falling in love at all is not extremely probable
she was affectionate and pleasing, and extremely fond of me

oewn-04848589-n.learner: kind and careful thought for other people.
examples: with due consideration for the advantage of all your family
It was owing to him, to his reserve and want of proper consideration

oewn-05831106-n.learner: something you should keep in mind when you are making a decision.
examples: I hope that no consideration with regard to this young man will influence her.

oewn-05792836-n.learner: the act of thinking about something carefully.
examples: The plan is still under consideration.

oewn-01638974-v.learner: to imagine something, or see it in your mind.
examples: When she was discontented, she fancied herself nervous.
a silence which might make him fancy her affected with what had passed

oewn-01780389-v.learner: to like or want something in particular.
examples: She fancied a walk in the garden before dinner.

oewn-00004475-n.learner: a living thing that can act on its own, or that may grow able to.
examples: Every living being on the island depends on the rain.
The club came into being last spring.
when he did speak, it seemed the effect of necessity rather than of choice

oewn-05798247-n.learner: the person or thing that is chosen.
examples: for the first evening she was his settled choice
she would have been his only choice, had fortune permitted it

oewn-05798949-n.learner: one of several things when only one of them can be chosen.
examples: Her only choice was to walk home in the rain.

oewn-00120483-v.learner: to make something become a certain way.

whose northern aspect rendered it delightful for summer

oewn-02332196-v.learner: to give someone something useful or needed.
examples: The neighbours rendered assistance to the family after the fire.

oewn-01736053-v.learner: to give your own interpretation or performance of something.
examples: She rendered the old song slowly and with great feeling.

oewn-02411715-v.learner: to be the one that comes after someone or something.

oewn-02529837-v.learner: to do what you were trying to do, or to reach the goal you wanted.
examples: if he were so, they could not succeed
